description: The code an Edit Features node writes from its edit list (#662). Jest checks editFeaturesCode writes each `code` from its `settings`; utk_curio/sandbox/tests/test_feature_edits.py runs each `code` against `input` and checks the features left, by `key`.

cases.name: a new node: no edits, so the input is handed on as it came
cases.code:
# Edit Features writes this code from its edit list: each edit, in the
# order it was made, on the features whose key is one of its ids. It is
# written again when the list changes.
return curio_edit_features(input_0, [])

cases.name: two buildings removed, by their building_id, from one layer of several
cases.code:
# Edit Features writes this code from its edit list: each edit, in the
# order it was made, on the features whose key is one of its ids. It is
# written again when the list changes.
return curio_edit_features(input_0, [
    {"op": "remove", "ids": [1, 3]},
], key="building_id", layer="table_osm_buildings")

cases.name: a value set, a removal, then the removal put back
cases.code:
# Edit Features writes this code from its edit list: each edit, in the
# order it was made, on the features whose key is one of its ids. It is
# written again when the list changes.
return curio_edit_features(input_0, [
    {"op": "set", "ids": [2], "column": "name", "value": "Tower \"B\""},
    {"op": "remove", "ids": [3]},
    {"op": "restore", "ids": [3]},
    {"op": "set", "ids": [1], "column": "height", "value": None},
], key="building_id", layer="table_osm_buildings")
